Title: Ambler man sent to prison for sexual assault of woman at gunpoint
Article_Text:
NORRISTOWN — An Ambler man showed no emotion as a judge sent him to prison on charges that he forced a woman at gunpoint to perform a sex act on him while they were at a local nature preserve.
“That conduct is not acceptable in our society. The victim was courageous in coming forward,” Montgomery County Judge Wendy G. Rothstein said as she sentenced Anderson Danilo Luna-Mazate to 6½ to 13 years in a state correctional institution.
With a consecutive three-year probationary period, Luna-Mazate, 20, of the 2100 block of Lincoln Drive, will be under court supervision for 16 years.
Luna-Mazate, 20, of the 2100 block of Lincoln Drive, did not address the judge and offered no expression of remorse before learning his fate. During the trial, Luna-Mazate claimed the sexual contact was consensual and that he did not have a weapon.
“The jury chose to reject that defense,” Rothstein reminded Luna-Mazate.
During the trial in June, a jury convicted Luna-Mazate of charges of involuntary deviate sexual intercourse by force, indecent assault by force, simple assault by physical menace and possession of a concealed weapon in connection with a July 2025 incident at the Wissahickon Waterfowl Preserve in Ambler.
With its verdict, the jury found that Luna-Mazate was in possession of a firearm while committing the sexual assault.
Rothstein recommended that state corrections officials place Luna-Mazate under sex offender supervision and order that he have no contact with the victim.
The victim, in a letter read in court by Assistant District Attorney Margot S. Weitz, stated, “I will never forget that night. It will always be circling in my mind.”
“You chose to cause me irreversible pain and trauma that I will have to live with the rest of my life. I am not the same woman I used to be, and you changed that,” the woman addressed Luna-Mazate directly in the victim impact statement, adding that her ability to trust others has been fractured.
Weitz argued for a sentence of 7 to 14 years’ imprisonment for Luna-Mazate, who prosecutors alleged brandished a gun when the 19-year-old woman spurned his sexual advances and he forced her to perform a sex act.
“This was a sexual assault. When she is saying, ‘No,’ he puts a gun to her head. There was a deadly weapon involved. Her lack of consent meant nothing to him. Her saying ‘No’ meant nothing to him,” Weitz argued during the sentencing hearing. “He poses a real risk to people in the community.”
Luna-Mazate also faces a lifetime requirement to report his address to state police in order to comply with Pennsylvania’s Sexual Offender Registration and Notification Act.
Prior to the sentencing hearing, Luna-Mazate was evaluated by the Pennsylvania Sexual Offenders Assessment Board, which determined he did not meet legal criteria to be classified as a sexually violent predator, a designation that imposes more stringent restrictions on offenders while they are on parole and probation, including mandatory counseling.
Defense lawyer Cary Hall argued for a more mitigated sentence of no more than five years in prison for Luna-Mazate.
“My client has no criminal history whatsoever. We ask the court for compassion and mercy for this young man who has his whole life ahead of him,” Hall argued.
Hall said Luna-Mazate was born in Guatemala and came to the U.S. to escape gang violence in his country, obtain an education and work so he could send money home to his family. According to Hall, Luna-Mazate, who shared a child with his girlfriend, was seeking asylum in the U.S. at the time of the incident. Hall conceded that Luna-Mazate likely will be deported after he completes his sentence in the U.S.
Hall presented the judge with 36 letters of support from Luna-Mazate’s relatives, friends and coworkers, who indicated they were “flabbergasted” by his arrest and who claimed the incident was out of character for the man they know.
“I cannot find justification for a mitigated sentence,” said Rothstein, turning down Hall’s request for mitigation.
Testimony and court documents indicate the woman met Luna-Mazate in mid-July at the Wissahickon Waterfowl Preserve and after a brief conversation the pair exchanged Instagram account information. Over the next couple of days, Luna-Mazate and the woman communicated via Instagram.
On the evening of July 26, 2025, Luna-Mazate used the Instagram app to call the woman and they agreed to meet to hang out at the nature preserve. Luna-Mazate and the woman sat in her vehicle that she parked in the unit block of North Maple Avenue directly in front of the walking trail for the preserve, according to the criminal complaint filed by Ambler Detective Tyler Conroy.
While inside the vehicle shortly after midnight on July 27, Luna-Mazate indicated he wanted to engage in sexual acts with the woman, who was in the driver’s seat, and he began to touch her as he was in the front passenger seat, authorities alleged.
“She verbalized numerous times that she did not want to do any sexual acts with the suspect and that she wanted him to stop,” Conroy alleged.
When the woman asked Luna-Mazate to stop touching her and to leave her vehicle, he retrieved a black firearm from his backpack, placed it on his lap and stated, “I don’t think you understand,” according to the arrest affidavit.
“He then began pointing the firearm in her direction,” Conroy alleged.
While he held the gun in one hand, Luna-Mazate pulled down his pants and with his other hand forced the woman to perform a sex act on him, detectives alleged.
Weitz argued Luna-Mazate used physical as well as emotional and psychological force against the victim.
The woman attempted to push Luna-Mazate away from her, and eventually Luna-Mazate released the woman from his grip. Luna-Mazate then masturbated as the woman repeatedly told him to get out of her vehicle, according to arrest documents.
Eventually, Luna-Mazate gathered his belongings, exited the woman’s vehicle, and walked away.
When Luna-Mazate entered the witness box in his own defense, he testified that the sexual contact was consensual and that he did not have a gun.
When confronted with Instagram photos he posted that depicted him displaying guns, he claimed that he owned fake guns and displayed photos with them in order to gain Instagram followers.
The woman contacted a female friend shortly after the incident and told her what had occurred in the vehicle.
The victim reported the incident to Ambler police on July 30.

Title: Main Line Health receives $1 million for project at Taylor Hospital
Article_Text:
Main Line Health was granted $1 million in state funding for potentially restarting emergency care at Taylor Hospital.
On Wednesday, state Rep. Dave Delloso, D-162, of Ridley Park, announced that $1 million of Local Share Account funding had been awarded to Main Line Health for a project at Taylor Hospital.
Main Line Health officials confirmed they are deliberating whether to expand emergency operations to the closed Ridley Park hospital.
Main Line Health Communications Officer Larry Hanover issued a statement.
“We are incredibly grateful to the Delaware County legislative delegation and the Governor’s Office for helping secure $1 million in funding to enhance access to patient care in the county,” it read. “Our state leaders have been exceedingly supportive and persistent as we respond to the increased patient volume resulting from the closure of Crozer Health last year. We are actively evaluating options, including Taylor Hospital, to expand our emergency care capacity and look forward to sharing more details as those plans develop.”
Delloso also addressed the funding and what he said it will bring to the Ridley Park area.
“Today I’m proud to announce that Main Line Health has been awarded $1 million in LSA grant funding for a future project at Taylor Hospital,” Delloso said. “Prospect Medical’s bankruptcy and subsequent closure have had devastating effects in Delaware County.
“My district, in particular, suffered significantly from the shutdown of Taylor Hospital,” he continued. “Taylor wasn’t just a health care provider but a major employer in the area, too. As is standard for private equity firms, services were cut to siphon larger profit margins for shareholders until patients and employees were left with nothing.”
Taylor Hospital, a part of Crozer Health, was closed in April 2025 by Crozer Health parent company Prospect Medical Holdings Inc. amid bankruptcy proceedings.
And, the next month, Crozer-Chester Medical Center was closed, the final hospital domino to fall as the for-profit Prospect completed the shuttering of its four hospitals along with the outpatient services offices, with all of it leaving many Delaware County residents in a health care desert.
Their vision is to bring a viable health care provider to the facility.
Attempts to reach the investors’ spokesman Wednesday were unsuccessful.
The $1 million comes from Local Share Account funding, which are monies provided through the Commonwealth Financing Authority to support projects that improve the quality of life for residents and communities across Pennsylvania.
“It will take years of continuous work to fully recover from the hospital closures that have plagued the county, but I am proud of the steps that my colleagues and I have taken toward that goal,” Delloso added.
Main Line Health reported a 41% increase in emergency room volume from March 2025 through May 2026. The system also reported the average emergency room patients per day was 170 in May compared to 121 in March 2025, the month before the last two Crozer hospitals closed.
“Minutes can mean the difference between life and death in an emergency, and making sure my constituents have access to critical care has been a top priority of mine,” Delloso said.
The state legislator expressed enthusiasm for what is to come.
“I look forward to seeing what developments are made with Taylor Hospital, and I will be sure to keep you updated,” Delloso said. “In the meantime, I will continue to push for tighter regulations to prevent parasitic equity firms from destroying necessary care systems in the future.”
Ridley Park Borough Manager Trish Hollabaugh said she spoke about the development at Tuesday’s borough council meeting.
“We’re very excited to see how this grant is going to pan out and is going to be beneficial to the residents,” she said. “I think it’s wonderful.”
Hollabaugh said borough officials don’t know what Main Line Health’s plans are for the facility but they are aware of how the Crozer Health closures have impacted their residents.
“It’s been difficult,” she said. “It’s been a hardship here.”
The borough manager said new services at the former hospital are well deserved for their residents.
“I’m very excited to see what happens,” she said.

Title: CDC delay holds up children's COVID vaccine orders | Honolulu Star-Advertiser
Article_Text:
CDC delay holds up children’s COVID vaccine orders
U.S. states are facing delays in obtaining COVID-19 vaccines for children through a federal immunization program, the Wall Street Journal reported today, citing people familiar with the matter.
The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has not started accepting orders for COVID-19 shots, according to the report.
States provide free vaccines to children through the Vaccines for Children program, which covers about half of the country’s youths, and to uninsured or underinsured adults through a separate government program.
Commercially insured patients can already get shots at pharmacies such as CVS.
Government orders for COVID-19 shots are typically placed within two weeks of the vaccines becoming available for commercially insured programs, the report added.
A U.S. Department of Health and Human Services spokesperson said COVID-19 does not follow the same predictable seasonal pattern as influenza and other respiratory viruses, and that an arbitrary September date should not be treated as a public health deadline for vaccine procurement.
Don't miss out on what's happening!
Stay in touch with breaking news, as it happens, conveniently in your email inbox. It's FREE!
The CDC is finalizing decisions on COVID-19 vaccine procurement through the Vaccines for Children and Section 317 programs, and more details will be available soon, the spokesperson added.
The holdup comes as the Trump administration scales back vaccine guidance. The CDC no longer recommends that all children get a COVID shot and is instead urging parents to consult their doctors. The agency had previously recommended that everyone age six months and older receive the vaccine.
A federal judge earlier this year blocked the administration from enacting a narrower vaccine schedule.
Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who has publicly criticized the COVID vaccine, has pushed the administration to broadly step back from vaccine recommendations.
Vaccine hesitancy is rising nationwide, and measles outbreaks are spreading, with four measles-related deaths reported in Pennsylvania earlier on Tuesday.
>> RELATED: GOP senator blames Trump vaccine policy for measles deaths
Demand for COVID booster shots has already fallen sharply, and fewer than 10% of children aged six months to 17 were vaccinated last year, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing CDC data.

Title: Mom Who Gave Teen $27K Prom Send-Off Jailed For PPP Fraud
Article_Text:
Mom Who Gave Teen $27K Prom Send-Off Jailed For PPP Fraud
Mom Who Gave Daughter $27K ‘Philly Princess’ Prom Send-Off Sentenced To Prison After $535K COVID Relief Fraud Case
Treva Harris was sentenced to federal prison after pleading guilty to bank fraud tied to a $535,000 PPP loan prosecutors say she obtained using false information and spent on personal expenses.
Share the post
Share this link via
Or copy link
Treva Harris, the Philadelphia mom who went viral in 2024 for spending a whopping $27,000 on a Cinderella-themed prom send-off for her daughter, was sentenced to 12 months and one day in federal prison for a $535,000 Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loan fraud scheme, according to a press release issued by U.S. Attorney’s Office, Eastern District of Pennsylvania on Sept. 11. The 50-year-old resident of Medford, New Jersey, was also ordered to serve three years of supervised release, a $7,500 fine, a $100 special assessment, and $535,000 in restitution by United States District Judge John F. Murphy.
RELATED CONTENT: From Private Jets To Pythons — 65 Lavish 2026 Black Prom Send-Offs Fueling Applause, Side-Eyes & Viral Discourse
Treva Harris PPP Loan Case: What happened?
The Paycheck Protection Program (“PPP”), established in 2020, was created by the federal government to provide emergency financial assistance to small businesses and their employees suffering the economic effects of the COVID-19 pandemic. However, federal prosecutors say Treva Harris used fraudulent information to obtain approximately $535,000 through the program and then spent much of the money on personal expenses unrelated to her Philadelphia childcare business, Child Prodigy Education Center (“CPEC”).
According to the press release, Harris applied for and received multiple pandemic-relief loans backed by the United States Small Business Administration (“SBA”) in 2020, including two loans associated with CPEC.
The first was an Economic Injury Disaster Loan (“EIDL”), which resulted in approximately $514,900 in disbursements to Harris. In an application submitted in April 2020, Harris reported that her childcare business had three employees, $165,907 in gross income during the previous 12 months and $113,420 in “cost of goods sold,” which prosecutors identified as payroll.
Just two months later, however, Harris submitted a separate PPP loan application for CPEC that included fabricated IRS documentation, according to prosecutors. In that application, Harris claimed that CPEC had 27 employees and a monthly payroll of $214,000, or $2,568,000 annually.
Based on the application, Harris received a $535,000 PPP loan. Federal prosecutors said much of the money was then spent on personal luxury retail purchases, large cash withdrawals and checks written to her boyfriend’s business.
Harris was charged by information in August 2025 and pleaded guilty in October to one count of bank fraud, waiving prosecution by indictment.
Read more about the case after the flip.
The case comes amid the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division.
The case comes amid a broader federal effort to investigate fraud involving COVID-era relief programs. On April 7, the Department of Justice announced the creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division (“Fraud Division”), which the department said would focus on investigating and prosecuting fraud against the American people.
“We fulfill our mission by using advanced data-driven investigative techniques; coordinating with agencies responsible for administering taxpayer-funded programs; partnering with federal, tribal, state, territorial, and local law enforcement on fraud-fighting efforts,” the department said of their mission on the DOJ website.
The effort supports President Trump’s Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a government-wide initiative chaired by Vice President J.D. Vance, targeting fraud, waste and abuse within federal benefit programs.
Treva Harris went viral in 2024 for creating a luxurious princess-themed prom send-off for her daughter.
Before her federal case, Harris drew attention in 2024 for an elaborate prom send-off for her daughter that transformed a Lancaster Avenue lot into a castle. The castle alone cost $27,000, according to 6abc Action News.
Harris described the elaborate setup as the home of a “Philly Princess” in a May 2024 Instagram post documenting the 12-hour transformation. According to the post, the setup began “at 5am and ended at approximately 5pm.”
She added, “Twelve hours of hard labor to birth what will forever be known as the Home of the ‘Philly Princess.'”

Title: Iowa Republicans in battleground House races vote to halt Iran war
Article_Text:
DES MOINES, Iowa — Two congressional Republicans in battleground Iowa districts, including one who recently campaigned alongside Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, changed their position on an Iran war powers resolution, joining with Democrats and a few other dissident members of their party in an attempt to halt President Donald Trump's ability to continue military action without lawmakers' approval.
The shift reflects the political pressure on Republicans before the November elections that will decide control of Congress. The war remains unpopular and has led to soaring fuel prices.
U.S. Reps. Zach Nunn and Mariannette Miller-Meeks voted for the resolution on Tuesday after previously voting against it.
“With the negotiating window closed, sustained combat operations now require congressional authorization,” Nunn, an Air Force veteran, posted on social media. “I will not support another open-ended war.”
Nunn campaigned with Hegseth last month in Iowa, and the Pentagon chief had lauded Nunn as an ally who didn't need any last-minute, late-night phone calls from Trump to persuade him to support the president's agenda.
“Zach Nunn is not a 3 a.m. congressman,” Hegseth said at a fundraiser for Nunn during the Iowa State Fair. “He’s willing to take the tough votes to do the right thing on behalf of our war fighters.”
Nunn is up against Sarah Trone Garriott in November's election.
Miller-Meeks, an Army veteran, said the president needs to present a plan to Congress and the public showing how the war ends.
“Americans do not want another forever war,” she said in a statement. “I will not vote to keep our soldiers in an open-ended war, with Iowans paying too much at the pump.”
She faces a reelection rematch against Christina Bohannan, whom she has defeated twice before.
The White House on Wednesday emphasized the administration's ongoing communication with Congress, including over 30 briefings to the Hill since February, “as we work toward this shared goal” of preventing a nuclear Iran.
“The administration has been fully transparent with Congress over the course of this conflict and throughout negotiations,” spokesperson Anna Kelly said in an email.
Voting shift reflects a growing weariness with the war
Both Republicans have advocated for Trump's actions in Iran as a deterrent against that country's nuclear capabilities. But their hesitation to see the prolonged conflict continue suggests that the impacts are increasingly wearing on Americans, and particularly Iowans. Eighteen U.S. service members have died in the war with Iran. Two are from Iowa, and one used to live in Iowa.
In addition to rising gasoline prices, diesel prices are reaching new highs just as U.S. farmers are ready to take their diesel-powered equipment to the fields for harvest.
National polling indicates that the Iran war remains unpopular with Americans overall. Only about 3 in 10 U.S. adults approved of Trump’s handling of Iran in a July AP-NORC poll, and a September New York Times/Siena poll found that about 6 in 10 likely voters think Trump’s decision to go to war with Iran was the wrong one.
Tuesday's House vote was the third time lawmakers voted to end the war in Iran. The margin was similar to earlier efforts, with a few more Republicans joining all Democrats in voting to end the conflict.
In addition to Nunn and Miller-Meeks, retiring U.S. Rep. Nancy Mace of South Carolina also shifted her position on the resolution. They joined Republican U.S. Reps. Tom Barrett of Michigan, Warren Davidson of Ohio, Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania and Thomas Massie of Kentucky, who had already been voting in favor.
Barrett and Fitzpatrick are both in battleground districts. Barrett, an Army veteran, said that he’s increasingly hearing skepticism in private conversations with others in his caucus.
“There’s a growing number of members that are having concerns about the growing nature of this without any congressional authorization,” Barrett said.
On Tuesday, though, the vast majority of House Republicans again rejected the resolution.
U.S. Rep. Ashley Hinson, who represents northeast Iowa but is running to replace retiring U.S. Sen. Joni Ernst, was one of the nays. Endorsed by Trump, Hinson faces Democrat Josh Turek for the seat, which Republicans are spending millions of dollars to defend.
Hinson acknowledged that she and other Americans want to see the war end. That means delivering a “decisive and immediate victory,” she said.
“I believe President Trump should immediately bring this war to a successful end in a way that keeps Americans safe from the threat of a nuclear armed Iran,” Hinson said in a statement.
Republicans are optimistic but watching Iowa closely
For months, Democrats targeting House and Senate seats in Iowa have criticized the Republican incumbents for their votes on the war in Iran as a rubber stamp for Trump.
Republicans say that Iowa, where Trump won overwhelmingly in the last three presidential elections, remains a red state that will help keep GOP majorities in both chambers. Republicans continue to outnumber Democrats statewide and in both Nunn’s and Miller-Meeks’ districts.
Still, the competitive races have gotten attention even from the White House. Trump visited suburbs of Des Moines for a rally in January and dispatched Vice President JD Vance in May to campaign for Nunn.
After Hegseth campaigned with Nunn, a group of more than 400 former national security officials filed a complaint requesting an investigation into whether the secretary violated the Hatch Act, which restricts political activities by federal officials.
Hegseth's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
___
Catalini reported from Morrisville, Pennsylvania. Associated Press reporter Nicholas Riccardi contributed from Lansing, Michigan.

Title: What to know about Ed Sheeran's tour after Macklemore was cut and other artists dropped out
Article_Text:
By Canadian Press on September 16, 2026.
Ed Sheeran’s tour of North and South America has been roiled by the decision this week to drop Macklemore as an opener because of the rapper’s onstage pro-Palestinian comments. Since then, all of Sheeran’s other supporting acts have dropped out, including a group that plays with Sheeran during part of the show.
Sheeran, who is scheduled to perform in Philadelphia on Saturday, said the decision to cut Macklemore from the Loop Tour was the promoter’s, not his own. The “Thrift Shop” rapper exclaimed “Free Palestine” during the Sept. 5 date in New Jersey.
“To all of my Jewish brothers and sisters, criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide, it in no way is criticism of you,” he said during the New Jersey concert. “This message is for peace, love, for all human beings to be treated with dignity, respect, and equality.”
Macklemore has said his removal was the result of an effort led by Robert Kraft, the billionaire owner of the New England Patriots. His Kraft Group also owns Gillette Stadium, where the NFL team plays and where Sheeran is scheduled to perform later this month. Kraft’s involvement was implicitly cited in some of the statements from the supporting acts who left Sheeran’s tour Tuesday, decrying the influence of money.
On Wednesday, Macklemore announced he would donate $1 million from his net earnings from the tour to six organizations helping Palestinians, including the U.N. agency for Palestinian refugees, UNRWA. He challenged Kraft to match the donation.
“Whatever we disagree about, perhaps we can agree on this: Palestinian lives are worth protecting,” Macklemore wrote.
Here’s where things stand with Sheeran’s tour.
Finneas, Lukas Graham, Aaron Rowe and Beoga all quit
The Danish band Lukas Graham and Irish singer Aaron Rowe were scheduled to replace Macklemore as the opening acts on Sheeran’s remaining U.S. tour dates. Finneas, the American singer and close collaborator with sister Billie Eilish, was down to open for Sheeran on four of his South American dates. Beoga, an Irish folk band, had been performing with Sheeran for part of his set since his tour began in January in New Zealand.
“Artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed,” Finneas wrote.
The announcements from each supporting act came roughly within an hour of each other Tuesday. Earlier that day, Sheeran posted his own statement blaming the promoter for Macklemore’s removal and maintaining that he refused to be drawn into a public discussion about the war in Gaza.
Rowe and Beoga cited their country’s history to explain their decision. “We are Irish people who understand colonialism. As founding members of the Irish Artists for Palestine movement, we are committed activists for justice and will continue to be,” Beoga posted.
Rowe called Sheeran a friend. “But as Irish people we know all too well about genocide, forced famine and violent occupation,” he wrote, adding that he couldn’t “stand by and allow billionaires to use their position of power to silence the rightful voices of those who speak up.”
Lukas Graham also appeared to take a veiled shot at Kraft, writing: “Money doesn’t give you the right to own the conversation. Nobody’s bank balance should decide who gets to speak or which suffering we’re allowed to acknowledge.”
Kraft’s representatives did not respond to emailed requests for comment Tuesday and Wednesday, but in a statement Monday, he wrote that the decision to cancel Macklemore was a result of the rapper’s recent comments “and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery.”
“This decision is not about diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians or denying anyone the right to advocate on their behalf. Their pain and loss are real,” Kraft said.
Sheeran hasn’t commented since the supporting acts dropped out
After Macklemore issued a lengthy statement Monday about being removed from the tour, Sheeran took to Instagram to lay out his side.
“Macklemore coming off tour was the promoter’s decision, it was not mine,” he wrote Tuesday. “I would never let down the fans who had made plans, nor would I abandon the touring crew and the other support acts and musicians who rely on me for work and to make a living.”
Sheeran hasn’t posted since those supporting acts left the tour, and his representative didn’t respond to an emailed request for comment. The promoter, Messina Touring Group, also hasn’t responded to requests for comment.
Macklemore on Wednesday didn’t address the fallout, writing instead that he wanted to “bring the conversation back to where it belongs: to the Palestinian people who are still being killed, still living under military occupation, and still fighting for their freedom.”
In his statement Tuesday, Sheeran said he was “not complicit” and that he had his own views on the war in Gaza.
“There is a reason I do not use my professional platform for politics — my audience includes young people, often children, of all backgrounds. Those who come to my show do not expect a political forum,” he wrote.
While Sheeran has not been as politically vocal as many fellow artists, he has expressed support for some causes in the past. He performed at the Concert for Ukraine in 2022, which raised money for Ukrainians affected by the Russian invasion, and collaborated with a Ukrainian band on a charity single. He has also campaigned against racism in the U.K. and criticized his country’s government for cutting arts funding.
The Associated Press

Title: Measles exposure in Sussex County, DE
Article_Text:
Delaware health officials warn residents of possible measles exposure in Rehoboth Beach, Sussex County
The warning comes after an out-of-state traveler visited the Rehoboth Beach area while contagious. Officials encourage residents to get vaccinated.
What are journalists missing from the state of Delaware? What would you most like WHYY News to cover? Let us know.
Delaware health officials are sounding the alarm after an out-of-state visitor with measles spent time in Sussex County earlier this month.
The state’s Division of Public Health was notified that the individual visited an unknown number of stores and restaurants in the greater Rehoboth Beach area Sept. 4. Officials said the person was not showing symptoms at the time but was believed to be contagious.
Because the state could not confirm all the locations the person visited, the Division of Public Health issued a community-wide notification Wednesday.
The news comes as Delaware is experiencing a measles outbreak. Currently, 23 cases have all been confirmed in Kent County. Before the recent surge, the state had not reported a measles case in more than a decade.
Officials recommend that people who were in the area Sept. 4 monitor themselves for early symptoms of measles. Symptoms include fever, cough, runny nose and pink eye lasting up to four days before a rash appears. The rash, a telltale sign of infection, typically appears three to five days after symptoms begin, starting on the face before spreading down the body.
Unvaccinated, pregnant, immunocompromised persons and children who are too young to be vaccinated are at higher risk of contracting and spreading the infectious disease.
People who develop these symptoms should immediately self-isolate and contact a health care provider to report their symptoms. If symptoms are severe, they should seek immediate medical care. Health officials said that people who suspect they have been infected should call ahead before visiting a health care facility so staff can prepare for their arrival.
Health officials encourage eligible residents to get vaccinated to protect themselves from contracting measles. Receiving two doses of the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine is 97% effective in preventing contraction and is the best form of protection, according to officials.
Residents can confirm whether they have been vaccinated against measles by confirming with their doctor or through the DelVAX Public Portal. Vaccinations are available at health care offices as well as the state’s public health clinics and mobile health units.
The U.S. is experiencing its largest measles outbreak since 1991. Cases surpassed 2025 totals in July. More than 3,300 cases have been reported so far in 46 states, with Pennsylvania leading the nation with 676 individual cases reported. The 23 cases in Kent County have been the only confirmed cases in Delaware so far.

Title: Ranking every 0-1 team in the NFL by their playoff chances
Article_Text:
Not all NFL playoff teams are created equally. Despite starting 0-1, there are still quite a few teams that can get into playoff contention. That said, not every 0-1 team will be good enough to land in the postseason.
Here’s a look at the teams that lost in Week 1 and how we feel about them still reaching the playoffs.
16. Miami Dolphins
Miami looked like a team that gutted its entire roster this offseason and a team that’s in the depths of a rebuild. The way Las Vegas made light work of them goes to show how far this team has to go to make the NFL playoffs. That’s not to say they can’t, but let’s be realistic here, they won’t. Every other AFC East team aside from the New England Patriots won in Week 1. The New York Jets look like a better team right now than the Dolphins do, which says a lot.
15. Cleveland Browns
The only reason Cleveland isn’t dead last is because once they figure out their quarterback, they will be a better team. Their winning quarterback isn’t on their roster, though, and their defense looked horrid in Week 1. It was always going to be a different type of defense without Myles Garrett and until they iron out their kinks of the new scheme, they’ll be at the bottom of the totem pole.
14. Tennessee Titans
It was a rough Week 1 in Nashville. The Titans still have a lot to work through, but they aren’t the worst team in the NFL after one game. They looked bad; that said, the AFC South could be up in the air. Maybe they turn things around, maybe they don't, but I wouldn’t have high hopes for Tennessee and doing anything other than struggling this season.
13. Atlanta Falcons
Until the Atlanta Falcons figure out their quarterback situation, they’re going to be on the outside of the playoff bubble. Cooper Rush isn’t going to be good enough to carry them to the playoffs, let alone a winning season. For what it’s worth, the only quarterback on the Falcons’ roster that might be good enough is Michael Penix Jr. and he’s still recovering from his torn ACL.
12. Los Angeles Chargers
Before the season, I would have expected the Los Angeles Chargers to be a playoff bubble team. After a debilitating loss to the Arizona Cardinals, I’m less optimistic. Mike McDaniel is the new offensive coordinator and the offense struggled a lot against Arizona. They could turn things around, but the AFC West looks like it will be a challenge again this year, which is exactly why the Chargers will struggle to make the playoffs.
11. Indianapolis Colts
It was a bad first game back from injury for Daniel Jones. It’s week one so I’m trying not to overreact too much, but it’s hard to look past how bad the Colts looked in Week 1. For now, the Colts aren’t passing the confidence meter. That said, for now it looks like the Jaguars will be their toughest battle. Houston isn’t bad, but can’t win the clutch, which will be a factor at the end of the year.
10. Carolina Panthers
The Carolina Panthers had a strong start to the season despite losing to the Chicago Bears. Bryce Young and the Panthers offense amassed more than 400 total yards and showed that the Panthers might not struggle as much people thought before the season. The Panthers could very well fall apart, but for now, you should be confident they’ll look better than they did last year.
9. Washington Commanders
Washington came back against Philadelphia but came up short of getting the win in Week 1. The Commanders have to look a lot better than they did a year ago and that will come down to Jayden Daniels’ health. They aren’t the same without him and Week 1 is proof of that. The NFC East is still up for grabs and the Commanders could very well contend in the division. Don’t let the loss to Philadelphia fool you.
8. Dallas Cowboys
The Cowboys have a lot to fix on defense, but they’re still a good team. I wouldn’t be out on them despite a loss to the New York Giants. New York looked inspired in Week 1. This division is going to be tougher than it has been in years past, which is why you can’t count any team out just yet, and certainly not after one game.
7. Houston Texans
It was not a good week for C.J. Stroud. Not only did the Texans stall his contract talks until after season, he also fell apart against the Buffalo Bills, fumbling the ball in the redzone and costing Houston a Week 1 win. Houston has made the playoffs every year since C.J. Stroud was drafted but that doesn’t necessarily mean they will this year. I’d be cautious about the Texans for now.
6. Green Bay Packers
Green Bay fell apart in Week 1, giving up 29 unanswered points in a Week 1, NFC North division loss to the Minnesota Vikings. The Packers are still a good team and should do well in the division. I wouldn’t let the fourth quarter collapse sway your judgement on the Packers. Unless it happens again, they should still be a good team this season.
5. New Orleans Saints
The New Orleans Saints looked like a team that just might get into the playoffs this year. They got down by 21 points against the Lions and were a two-point try away from completing the comeback. Every team in the NFC South lost this week but there’s no reason why the Saints shouldn’t contend in the division this year.
4. Tampa Bay Buccaneers
Tampa Bay had some ball security problems in Week 1. When they didn’t turn the ball over, though, the offense didn’t look like it missed Mike Evans. Baker Mayfield has his extension so that’s not looming over this team either. The NFC South is open and it will probably come down to the Bucs and the Saints.
3. Denver Broncos
Denver had a very rough start to 2026, which should be expected considering Sean Payton gave up play-calling duties. It’s going to take time for Davis Webb and Bo Nix to get in sync. Don’t judge Denver on the first few weeks as they look to get the offense on track. That said, they can’t fall to 0-2 either. For now, they’re still a playoff lock, but things can change rapidly.
2. New England Patriots
Drake Maye was having fits with the Seattle defense once again to start the season. That said, that was the only problem for the Patriots, considering they only lost 13-10. No need to press the panic button just yet. New England should still contend in the AFC East and should still be a playoff team, but it won’t be easy either.
1. Los Angeles Rams
Los Angeles has made the playoffs in all but one year with Matthew Stafford. They should be back in the postseason this year too. They did all of that without Myles Garrett so the fact that they won’t have him for at least the next four games shouldn’t be too much of a problem. This is still a good team, and they’re still a dangerous team in the NFC.

Title: R1 Unveils Phare Utilization Management on Phare OS to Eliminate Medical Necessity Denials
Article_Text:
What You Should Know
- Healthcare revenue cycle management leader R1 announced the launch of Phare Utilization Management (Phare UM), an AI-enabled solution moving hospital utilization management from retrospective chart auditing to proactive, real-time decisioning.
- The Guthrie Clinic—a non-profit, integrated health system serving northern Pennsylvania and upstate New York—is among the first health systems to deploy Phare UM across its acute care operations.
- Built directly on Phare OS, R1’s core pre-bill intelligence platform, to continuously evaluate 100% of patient encounters from admission through discharge, replacing manual sampling that traditionally reviews only a fraction of high-risk admissions.
- Integrates Phare Intelligence with R1’s proprietary Payer Atlas to cross-reference real-world payer claim histories, clinical criteria, hospital payer mix, and institutional denial tolerance to prioritize reviews by financial risk rather than admission chronology.
Continuous 100% Encounter Review and Payer-Specific Risk
Rather than relying on spot checks or manual worklists, Phare UM integrates clinical criteria with longitudinal reimbursement data:
- Comprehensive Case Evaluation: Evaluates every patient encounter across the hospital stay using Phare Intelligence, identifying documentation deficiencies and clinical risk while the patient is still admitted and notes can be clarified.
- Payer Atlas Risk Calibration: Integrates payer-specific contract terms, local medical necessity policies, and historical denial trends to rank cases by audit likelihood and denial vulnerability, prioritizing worklists based on true financial and clinical risk rather than admission timestamp.
- Quantified Inpatient vs. Observation Scenarios: Leverages R1’s database of historical payer outcomes to project audit outcomes. In an early customer assessment, Phare UM identified that approximately 65% of observation encounters met the threshold to be billed as inpatient stays, revealing substantial revenue leakage and statusing inaccuracies.
Augmenting Clinical Judgment with Physician Advisory Integration
Phare UM functions as a decision-support layer designed to support hospital UM nurses and physician advisors rather than replace human determination:
- Longitudinal Context Preservation: Unifies case context across clinical reviews, peer-to-peer discussions, secondary reviews, and downstream appeals so reviewers have an auditable evidentiary trail without toggling across disconnected systems.
- Physician Advisory Workflows: Integrates directly into R1’s Physician Advisory Services (PAS) operations, surfacing condensed clinical summaries and evidence citations to accelerate level-of-care determinations and peer-to-peer defense.
“Healthcare organizations have too many critical decisions occurring in disconnected workflows across the patient and financial journey,” said Joe Flanagan, Chief Executive Officer of R1. “Our vision for Phare OS is to create the industry’s most intelligent and integrated pre-bill architecture, connecting the revenue cycle through a shared foundation of clinical, financial and operational intelligence. Phare UM brings that vision to life in utilization management by helping organizations reduce friction, spot risk sooner, close documentation gaps earlier, and reduce avoidable medical necessity denials.”
Expanding the Pre-Bill Architecture
The launch marks a key step in R1’s strategy to build a unified mid-revenue cycle platform. By linking Phare UM with prior authorizations, clinical documentation integrity (CDI), and autonomous inpatient coding, R1 aims to eliminate the administrative handoffs between clinical documentation and claim submission—intercepting denials before initial billing.

Title: M&A: MRO Acquires Vyne Medical to Expand Intelligent Healthcare Intake Automation
Article_Text:
What You Should Know
- Healthcare clinical data management leader MRO announced it acquired Vyne Medical, a specialist in healthcare data intake and intelligent document processing (IDP) serving more than 800 hospitals nationwide.
- The transaction scales MRO’s enterprise market footprint to serve more than 2,500 hospitals and 35,000 ambulatory clinics, creating a unified clinical data pipeline across the patient encounter lifecycle.
- Vyne Medical specializes in converting unstructured information—spanning analog paper records, incoming faxes, medical images, and recorded voice conversations—into discrete, structured data for downstream electronic medical record (EMR) and revenue cycle workflows.
- The combined platform pairs machine-learning automation for data extraction, classification, and routing with human-in-the-loop clinical specialists to maintain compliance and accuracy without overburdening health system staff.
- Vyne Medical will operate under the transitional brand identity “Vyne Medical, an MRO Company.”
Consolidating Front-Door Intake with Enterprise HIM Release of Information
Norristown, Pennsylvania-based MRO (backed by Parthenon Capital) is historically known for enterprise release of information (ROI), payer audit management, and clinical data exchange across health systems. The acquisition of Vyne Medical—operating during the transition period as “Vyne Medical, an MRO Company”—bridges MRO’s downstream exchange infrastructure with Vyne’s front-end clinical intake and patient access workflows:
- Scale Across Acute and Ambulatory Sites: The combined company will support more than 2,500 hospitals and 35,000 ambulatory clinics, creating one of the largest clinical data management footprints in the U.S.
- Unstructured-to-Discrete Conversion: Incorporates Vyne’s communication and document capture tools (such as its Trace platform) to extract unstructured inputs across faxes, phone audio recordings, and scanned images, converting them into structured, discrete clinical data.
- Hybrid Automation and Clinical Governance: Pairs algorithmic document classification and optical character recognition (OCR) with MRO’s specialized operational teams to review ambiguous or complex charts, ensuring data accuracy before information is committed to the EMR or sent downstream to payers.
Closing the Upstream Data Leakage Loop
The transaction reflects an ongoing consolidation across healthcare document management and revenue cycle infrastructure. As health systems face mounting margin pressure and administrative labor shortages, hospitals are moving away from managing separate vendors for digital fax intake, voice call recording, medical record indexing, and ROI fulfillment.
“Some of the most valuable data in a health system is often trapped in a fax, a phone call, or a scanned document outside the EMR, invisible to the teams who need it, and regularly rekeyed by hand to inform another workflow,” said Jason Brown, CEO of MRO. “By adding Vyne Medical’s capabilities, we can capture that information at the ‘front door’ when it enters a provider’s workflow, curate it into discrete, structured clinical data, and exchange it wherever it needs to go, making that data accessible and intelligent so they can take the appropriate action.”
By capturing clinical documentation at the point of ingestion and translating it into discrete data elements, MRO can feed cleaner clinical context into mid-revenue cycle operations (such as utilization review, clinical documentation integrity, and prior authorization), directly reducing the manual chart-chasing that drives up the cost-to-collect.

Title: AOC accuses Robert Kraft of trying to censor Macklemore's free speech
Article_Text:
Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez has added her voice to the chaos and the “geopolitical fight” surrounding the remaining U.S. dates of Ed Sheeran’s world tour, after Macklemore was dropped as the act and four other artists announced Tuesday that they were pulling out of the trek in support of the rapper’s right to speak out on behalf of Palestinians in Gaza.
From Ocasio-Cortez’s perspective, the controversy isn’t just about Macklemore, the fate of Sheeran’s Loop Tour, or the plight of Palestinians in Gaza. During an interview outside the U.S. Capitol, the New York City representative said it raises serious concerns about free speech and sets “a dangerous precedent.” She, too, raised concerns about reports that New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft had lined up other stadium owners to prevent Macklemore from performing in their venues and from expressing his views on an important global issue.
In clips played by Fox News and TMZ, Ocasio-Cortez said: “It’s not just what has happened with the act and not just in removing Macklemore from the lineup, but when you see what Robert Kraft did to line up all of the stadiums to censor speech in that one specific way, it’s become clear that this is not just about one music artist or two music artists, but this is about how just a handful of stadium owners and the elite can prevent an entire massive issue, in this case, the genocide in Gaza (from being talked about).”
Ocasio-Cortez said it might not “stop there,” with artists expressing views on this particular issue. “It could be speaking out about A.I.,” she said. “It could be speaking out about any issue that you can get a handful of stadium owners to ensure that an entire person’s career can be jeopardized if they speak out about any issue.”
🗣️ Rep. AOC tells @hicharliecotton she is boycotting Ed Sheeran because she says he's complicit in Robert Kraft and other stadium owners' efforts to silence Macklemore. pic.twitter.com/zuISc3zaFs
— TMZ (@TMZ) September 15, 2026
The congresswoman admitted that she was not inclined to listen to Sheeran’s music at the present time, though she was hesitant to say whether she thought he was complicit in the controversy because she does not know about how much control that he has in decisions over his own shows, as Axios has reported. “I have have no idea what the financial entanglements of all of that is,” Ocasio-Cortez said.
For his part, Sheeran said Tuesday that the decision to remove Macklemore from his tour came from promoters, not him. On Instagram, he expressed his sadness and horror over the “suffering and pain” occurring on both sides in “the conflict between Israel and Palestine.” But the English singer-songwriter insisted he didn’t want his tour to be drawn into a public discussion about the war.
Unfortunately for Sheeran, his tour already is mired in this discussion, as Ocasio-Cortez also noted. While she expressed empathy for his situation, she suggested that the global superstar could at least speak out “about this abuse of power” when it comes to the suppression of free speech.
“If they’re saying that to him, then they can say it to anybody. And at what point does it stop?” Ocasio-Cortez said before pivoting back to the people she sees as most responsible: “Robert Kraft and, you know, the actual people who are who are kind of twisting things here. So, and again, everyone has responsibility in the situation, everyone plays a role, but we need to be very clear about how dangerous a precedent this is.”
Indeed, the controversy potentially raises First Amendment issues if it turns out that certain venues barred Macklemore over his statements, as Rolling Stone reported.
Macklemore was booked to appear at eight of the 10 shows left on the U.S. leg of Sheeran’s tour, which is set to resume Friday in Philadelphia, Rolling Stone reported. In addition to the Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, which is privately owned by the Kraft Group, the other venues that allegedly objected to the rapper include: Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia; Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta; Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis; Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, North Carolina; AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas; and Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida. Most of these stadiums did not return Rolling Stone’s requests for comment.
In addition to Gillette Stadium, the Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte is privately owned. But the others are owned and/or operated by cities, states or other government entities, which is where the First Amendment comes in, according to Rolling Stone. Government entities in the United States can’t be seen as restricting speech, no matter how objectionable that speech may be.
The Hillsborough County-owned Raymond James Stadium in Tampa had to grapple with First Amendment concerns earlier this summer, when it had to allow two Kanye West concerts to proceed, despite calls for cancellation over his past antisemitic statements, Rolling Stone reported.
The controversy over Macklemore’s First Amendment rights possibly being restricted began earlier this month after the Seattle rapper appeared as the opening act for two of Sheeran’s shows at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, as Rolling Stone and Axios recounted. At the first show, Macklemore said he wanted to do the tour so he could “say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: ‘Free Palestine.’” He also expressed solidarity with people in Gaza, showed images of the war-torn Palestinian territory and performed his protest song, “Hind’s Hall,” about pro-Palestine demonstrators at Columbia University.
Macklemore’s remarks spurred immediate backlash and criticism from pro-Israel groups, who accused the rapper of ambushing fans with “anti-Israel propaganda,” Rolling Stone also reported. The singer Pink also voiced concerns. In a multi-part statement on Instagram, she said that as a Jewish person and “as a Jewish mom,” the rapper’s comments alarmed her, “and it scared people I love.”
At his second MetLife show, Macklemore addressed Jewish members of the audience, Rolling Stone also reported. He said, “Criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide in no way is a criticism of you.”
Sheeran’s tour began to spiral out of control this week when news came that Macklemore was being dropped from the tour, Axios reported. The tour’s promoters, Messina Touring Group, told Rolling Stone that concert venues had threatened to cancel Sheeran’s upcoming shows unless Macklemore was dropped as the opening act.
Macklemore claimed on Instagram that Kraft put pressure on Sheeran and the tour organizers to drop him from the show, particularly ahead of the singer’s performance at Kraft’s Gillette Stadium.
“Ed told me that Kraft said I would not be allowed to perform in his stadium,” Macklemore wrote. “Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: If Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues.”
Kraft issued a statement, confirming that he had made the decision to bar Macklemore from performing at Gillette. He said his decision was based on “material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran’s shows in New Jersey, and a broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community.” Kraft, however, did not address the rapper’s claim that he “rallied” other stadium owners to pressure Sheeran into dropping the performer, according to Rolling Stone.
With Macklemore’s removal from Sheeran, other artists who were scheduled to open for Sheeran also withdrew, including Finneas, Lukas Graham, and Aaron Rowe. Finneas, the singer-songwriter best known for his work with sister Billie Eilish, was scheduled to tour with Sheeran in South America later this year, but said on Instagram that “artists must not be silenced when they speak up for the oppressed.”
On social media, Danish pop artist Graham echoed Ocasio-Cortez’s concerns about rich and powerful business owners suppressing people’s ability “to speak about war, about civilians being killed, about children who deserve to grow up.” He added, “Money doesn’t give you the right to own the conversation. Nobody’s bank balance should decide who gets to speak or which suffering we’re allowed to acknowledge.”
